chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman al-Minqari, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubaydullah, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked, 'Which of the deeds is most superior in the presence of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no deed, after the recognition of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the recognition of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), that is more superior than hatred of the world. For that [hatred] are many branches, and for the disobediences are branches.'
So the first thing with which Allah was disobeyed was arrogance, the disobedience of Iblis when he refused and was arrogant, and he was of the disbelievers.

Then [comes] greed, and it is the disobedience of Adam and Hawwa (peace be upon them) when Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said to them, 'Eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you become of the unjust.' So they took what they had no need for, and that entered into their offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and that is that most of what the son of Adam seeks is what he has no need for.

Then [comes] envy, and it is the disobedience of the son of Adam when he envied his brother and killed him. So from that branched out the love of women, and the love of the world, and the love of leadership, and the love of comfort, and the love of speech, and the love of exaltedness and wealth. Thus they became seven traits, and they all gathered in the love of the world.
So the Prophets and the Scholars said after recognizing that: 'The love of the world is the head of every sin, and the world is two worlds: a world of bare necessities and a condemned world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed after knowing Allah according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that hatred of the world (bukh' al-dunya) is the supreme deed following divine recognition, tracing spiritual decline from Iblis's arrogance to Adam's greed and Cain's envy. It identifies the love of the world as the root of seven specific vices, culminating in the Prophetic and Scholarly consensus that it is the 'head of all sin,' distinguishing between the world of provision and the accursed world of distraction.
